commitResults.messageTitle: Add selection status to players
commitResults.messageBody:
Coaches running trials need to record whether each player is kept or
cut, but a player only holds a name and phone number.

Let's give every player a selection status of pending, kept or cut.
New players start as pending. The status is saved with the player,
and data files from v1.3, which have no status, load as pending.

Editing a player keeps their status, as edit is not meant to undo a
selection decision.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add keep, cut and pending commands
commitResults.messageBody:
Coaches have no way to set a player's selection status, and the list
does not show it.

Let's add the keep, cut and pending commands, which set the status of
the player at the given index in the displayed list. They share one
SetStatusCommand, as they differ only in the status they set. The
displayed list is not reset, so a coach can keep working through the
results of a find.

Each player card shows the status as a badge. The badge always shows
the status as text, so it does not rely on colour alone.

commitResults.messageTitle: Make add, edit and index errors point at the real problem
commitResults.messageBody:
Several input mistakes gave errors that blamed the wrong thing:

* add and edit read r/ or i/ as part of the value before it, so
  "add n/Pat p/8123 r/note" blamed the phone number (#129).
* An index of 0 or -1 gave a format error, while 99 gave an invalid
  index error (#130).
* A repeated prefix gave AB3's "single-valued field(s)" wording
  (#131).
* add silently kept the last of a repeated n/, p/ or j/, while edit
  rejected it (#132).

Let's reject remarks and injury statuses in add and edit with a
pointer to the right command, report any whole number that is not a
valid index as an invalid index, reword the repeated-prefix error,
and make add reject repeated prefixes like edit does.

Fixes #129, Fixes #130, Fixes #131, Fixes #132

commitResults.messageTitle: Accept real-world names and phones, and warn on similar names
commitResults.messageBody:
Coaches could not record many real players:

* Names with accented or non-English letters, commas or brackets,
  e.g. "José García" or "Lim Ah Kow (Ah Boy)", were rejected (#133).
* Phone numbers with brackets or dots, e.g. "(65) 9123 4567", were
  rejected, although spaces and hyphens were accepted (#134).

Also, "TanWei Ming" was added next to "Tan Wei Ming" without any
warning, although it is likely the same player (#135).

Let's accept any Unicode letter plus , ( ) in names, strip dots and
brackets from phone numbers like spaces and hyphens, and warn (but
still add) when a new name matches an existing one once spaces and
punctuation are ignored.

Fixes #133, Fixes #134, Fixes #135

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep the search after edit and say what edit changed
commitResults.messageBody:
After editing a search result, edit showed the full team again, so
the next index pointed at a different player than the coach expected
(#136). keep, cut, remark and injury already keep the search.

edit's message also hid some changes (#137). Removing a jersey number
or clearing tags looked the same as editing nothing, because the
message leaves out empty details, and an edit that changed nothing
still said "Edited player".

Let's keep the displayed list after edit, note a removed jersey number
or cleared tags in the message, and report when nothing changed.

Fixes #136, Fixes #137

commitResults.messageTitle: Name the actual problem in tag errors and allow more symbols
commitResults.messageBody:
Every invalid tag gave the same long message listing all the rules,
whether the tag was empty, too long, started with a symbol or had a
bad character, so coaches had to work out which rule they broke
(#138).

Tags also rejected symbols that coaches use in position and group
names, such as "Centre Back/Wing", "U18 & Under" or "Défenseur"
(#139).

Let's give a specific message for each problem, naming the tag and
the offending character, and allow accented letters and the symbols
& / _ + ' . in tags. As "/" is now allowed, text that looks like
another parameter, e.g. "filter t/Striker p/123", is rejected so the
typo is not silently read as part of the tag.

Fixes #138, Fixes #139

commitResults.messageTitle: Highlight injured players and let filter find them
commitResults.messageBody:
Injured players were hard to spot and impossible to list:

* Every card showed a plain "Injury status: fit" or "injured" line in
  the same style, so the coach had to read every card (#140).
* filter only accepted tags, so there was no way to see only the

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep tag equality and hashing consistent for Unicode letters
commitResults.messageBody:
Ian found two problems with the newly allowed Unicode tags:

* Tag#equals used equalsIgnoreCase but hashCode lower-cased the whole
  string, which can disagree, e.g. "İleri" and "ileri" were equal but
  hashed differently. "filter t/ileri" then missed a player tagged
  "İleri", and "t/İleri t/ileri" kept both tags.
* The first-character check looked at the first UTF-16 unit, so a
  tag starting with a letter outside the Basic Multilingual Plane,
  e.g. "𠀀 Team", was rejected.

Let's compare and hash the same case-folded form of the label, check
the first code point, and count the length in code points.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document deletion, selection decisions and saving in the UG
commitResults.messageBody:
The User Guide's sections for delete, keep/cut/pending, squad, saving
and the data file did not cover how the commands interact with search,
filter, squad and rating-sort views, and some statements were wrong.
For example, it said a deleted data folder makes saving fail, but
CouchCoach recreates the folder and saves normally.

Let's describe the verified behaviour of each command: which indices
they use, how the displayed list changes, the exact messages and
errors, and what is saved. Let's also explain what happens at startup
for missing, invalid and older data files, list the data file's
fields, add FAQ entries on data transfer and recovery, and record the
two startup crashes on null data and preferences as known issues.

commitResults.messageTitle: Rewrite the DG Storage component with up-to-date diagrams
commitResults.messageBody:
The Storage section's class diagram showed only three of the eight
fields JsonAdaptedPerson saves. It was a hand-drawn SVG and PNG, with a
separate PlantUML file that nothing used. The text did not explain how
the team is loaded at startup, or when and how saving happens.

Let's replace the images with a PlantUML class diagram showing every
saved field, and add activity diagrams for loading at startup and for
saving after a command. Let's also explain JSON adaptation, defaults
for older files, validation, the difference between in-memory and
saved changes, save failures, and the two main design choices.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document selection, deletion and saving use cases and manual tests
commitResults.messageBody:
The Selection status section listed fewer fields than withSelectionStatus
keeps, and did not explain how the squad view works. UC01 and UC05
described planned behaviour and cited user story IDs that the user
story table does not have. The Deleting and Saving manual tests were
still AB3 placeholders.

Let's add how squad works and why it is a predicate on the displayed
list, rewrite UC01 and UC05 to match the implemented behaviour, and
replace the placeholders with concrete tests for deleting, selection
and squad, and saving data, each with setup and cleanup.

commitResults.messageTitle: Implement add command for players
commitResults.messageBody:
Reduce the player record to a name and phone number, as required by
MVP feature F1, and remove the now unused email, address and tag
fields and classes.

Names are trimmed with repeated internal spaces collapsed, may contain
letters, digits, spaces and - ' / . and are limited to 100 characters.
Phones allow an optional leading '+' and 3 to 15 digits, with spaces
and hyphens stripped before storing.

Two players are duplicates if their names match ignoring case and
repeated spaces; the phone number is not compared. A repeated prefix
in add now takes its last value instead of being rejected.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add JerseyNumber to represent a player's jersey number
commitResults.messageBody:
Coaches identify players by their jersey numbers in trial notes and
videos, but there is no way to represent one yet.

Add a JerseyNumber class that accepts whole numbers from 0 to 99. A
leading zero is dropped so that "07" and "7" are the same number.

commitResults.messageTitle: Store an optional jersey number for each player
commitResults.messageBody:
Each player should be able to carry a jersey number, but Person and
its saved form only hold a name and a phone number.

Let's
* add an optional jersey number to Person, kept as a constructor
  without it for players who have none
* save the jersey number with the player, leaving the field out when
  the player has none

Data files saved by v1.3 have no jersey number field, so they still
load, with no player having a jersey number.

commitResults.messageTitle: Let add take an optional jersey number
commitResults.messageBody:
Coaches want to record a player's jersey number when they add the
player, but add only takes a name and a phone number.

Let's
* add a j/ prefix that add accepts as an optional jersey number
* show the jersey number in the player details of result messages

As with the other add fields, the last j/ value is used if the prefix
is repeated.

commitResults.messageTitle: Let edit change or remove a player's jersey number
commitResults.messageBody:
Coaches need to fix a jersey number after adding a player, or remove
it when the player gives the number up, but edit cannot change it.

Let's
* let edit take j/JERSEY to change the jersey number
* treat an empty j/ as removing the jersey number

EditPersonDescriptor tracks whether the jersey number was edited,
because a null jersey number alone cannot tell "leave it unchanged"
apart from "remove it".

commitResults.messageTitle: Show jersey numbers on player cards and in the help panel
commitResults.messageBody:
Jersey numbers can be added and edited, but coaches cannot see them
in the player list, and the help panel does not say how to set them.

Let's
* show "Jersey #N" on the card of each player that has a jersey number,
  hiding the line for players without one
* add [j/JERSEY] to add in the help panel, together with an edit entry
  that explains how to change or remove a jersey number
* give most sample players a jersey number, so that new users see the
  field in use

commitResults.messageTitle: Add Person#hasSameJerseyNumber to compare jersey numbers
commitResults.messageBody:
Commands need to find other players who wear the same jersey number,
but comparing two optional jersey numbers is easy to get wrong when
one or both players have none.

Add Person#hasSameJerseyNumber, which is true only when both players
have a jersey number and it is the same number.

commitResults.messageTitle: Warn the coach when two players share a jersey number
commitResults.messageBody:
Two players with the same jersey number usually means a typo, but add
and edit accept it silently, so the mistake goes unnoticed.

Let's
* let add and edit still make the change, but append a warning that
  names the other players with the same jersey number
* only warn on edit when the edit sets the jersey number, so editing
  other details of such a player does not repeat the warning

The change is not rejected because teams can reuse a number, e.g.
for players in different squads.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document jersey numbers in the user guide
commitResults.messageBody:
The user guide does not mention the j/ prefix, so coaches cannot
learn how to record, change or remove a jersey number.

Let's
* add [j/JERSEY] to the add and edit formats, with its rules and
  examples
* explain that an empty j/ removes the jersey number
* describe the warning shown when players share a jersey number
* update the command summary

commitResults.messageTitle: Show the saved jersey number in the storage class diagram

The DG does not show what JsonAdaptedPerson saves, and still says each

Let's
* show the fields of JsonAdaptedPerson in StorageClassDiagram, with a
  note that the jersey number is left out when a player has none
* explain in the Storage section how optional fields are saved, so
  that older data files still load
* mention the optional jersey number in the Model section

Let's
* add StorageClassDiagram.png, a redrawn class diagram that shows the

teammates can edit.

Tags, ratings, selection status, remarks and injury status were added

Let's
* add the jersey number to the full Person constructor and to every
  with* copy method, plus a new Person#withJerseyNumber
* keep the jersey number when RateCommand rebuilds a rated player,
  which would otherwise drop it
* save the jersey number with the other optional fields, leaving only
  that field out when it is absent, so other fields save as before
* show j/ alongside t/ in the add and edit help entries

commitResults.messageTitle: Test that jersey numbers survive a JSON round trip

so it does not check the JSON that is actually written to disk.

Add a test that serializes players with JsonUtil and reads them back,
checking that j/07 is written as 7 and that a player without a jersey
number is written without the jerseyNumber field.

* check that 0 is only shared with another 0, not with no number
* check that a teammate hidden by find is still named in the warning

commitResults.messageTitle: Enable assertions when running the app with Gradle
commitResults.messageBody:
Java assertions are off by default. Gradle turns them on for tests,
but not for the run task, so assert statements are never checked when
the app is launched with `./gradlew run`.

Turn them on in the run task so that broken assumptions fail fast
during local runs.

commitResults.messageTitle: Size player cards for their actual width A card with a long remark leaves a blank gap below its tags. The card's HBox root measures its height at the GridPane's preferred width of 150 instead of the width the card is given, so the remark is measured as if it wrapped over several lines.
commitResults.messageBody:
Let's use a VBox root, which measures its content at the given width,
so the card is only as tall as its content.

commitResults.messageTitle: Wrap long names instead of hiding the card badges When a name is too long for the card, the name row's HBox shrinks every label in it, so the Kept/Cut/Pending and Injured badges are cut down to "...".
commitResults.messageBody:

* keep each badge at its full width
* wrap the name onto more lines instead
* lay the row out in a GridPane, which sizes the row for the wrapped
  name, unlike an HBox

commitResults.messageTitle: Accept sort parameters in any letter case sort accepts its field and direction only in lower case, so `sort Rating` and `sort rating ASC` are rejected, while other parameters such as `injury 1 i/INJURED` accept any case.
commitResults.messageBody:
Let's match `rating`, `asc` and `desc` regardless of case. The command
word itself stays case-sensitive, like every other command.

commitResults.messageTitle: Let rate remove a player's rating Once a player is rated there is no way back to Unrated, e.g. after rating the wrong player, short of deleting and re-adding them.
commitResults.messageBody:
Let's accept `unrated`, in any letter case, in place of the score, so
`rate INDEX unrated` makes the player Unrated again. Rating a player
who is already unrated says so and changes nothing, like `injury` does
for a repeated status. An invalid score now also says how to remove a
rating.

commitResults.messageTitle: Let find match name parts joined by punctuation find matches only whole words split at spaces, so `find Ming`, `find Neil` and `find Jr` cannot find `Tan Wei-Ming`, `Shaun O'Neil` or `Lim Jr.`.
commitResults.messageBody:
Let's also match a keyword against each part of a word between
punctuation. The whole word still matches, so `find Wei-Ming` and
`find s/o` work as before, and each part must still match in full.

commitResults.messageTitle: Clarify active sorting in filter documentation
commitResults.messageBody:
The filter guide promises roster order even when a rating sort is active.
Document the retained sort, displayed indices and list reset behavior,
and include a concrete sorted-filter example.

commitResults.messageTitle: Wrap long command feedback in the result display
commitResults.messageBody:
Long duplicate-jersey warnings extend beyond the visible result area.
Enable text wrapping so the full warning can be read with vertical
scrolling at narrower window sizes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Accept tabs before command prefixes
commitResults.messageBody:
Pasted add, edit and filter commands reject tabs where spaces work.
Recognize spaces and tabs as prefix separators without changing field
contents or accepting joined prefixes and line breaks as delimiters.
Cover parser equivalence, duplicate prefixes and tokenizer boundaries.

commitResults.messageTitle: Allow safe saves after an applied command
commitResults.messageBody:
A save failure leaves delete in the command box after removing a player.
Pressing Enter again can delete the next player at the same index.

Return the applied command feedback with a save warning so the input
clears. Add save to persist the current team without repeating changes,
and explain recovery in the guide and command summary.

commitResults.messageTitle: Cover failed saves and safe retry through the UI
commitResults.messageBody:
Exercise an applied deletion with an obstructed data path, another Enter
press, repeated failed saves and a successful retry. Verify remaining
players, saved data and the sorted filtered view are preserved.

Update save-warning expectations and cover save syntax, an empty roster
and recovery guidance in the help panel.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep prefix scans within the argument string
commitResults.messageBody:
Scanning by prefix occurrence can overrun or loop for an empty prefix.
Scan separator positions instead, preserving the original tokenizer
boundary behavior while accepting tabs. Cover empty input explicitly.
